title: This Goose Flies Over the Himalayas Where Air Is Half Empty
subject: bar-headed goose

scenes.text: A goose flies over the Himalayas. How does it even breathe up there?
Bar-headed geese have been tracked at about seven thousand meters, where the air holds only thirty to fifty percent of sea-level oxygen.
Scientists made them fly in a wind tunnel wearing masks. Their hearts didn't speed up.
They slow their metabolism to match the thin air, and their blood cools by over two degrees, which helps it grab more oxygen.
In the wild they roll along the mountains like a roller coaster, because denser air is cheaper to fly in.
So the trick isn't flying high. It's knowing when to fly low.

description:
A goose crosses the Himalayas where the air has a fraction of the oxygen.
In a wind tunnel with a mask, its heart didn't even speed up.
Would you have guessed the trick is flying low?
